title: Concept: Response header built from a non-literal value in javascript — review required
description: In javascript, res.setHeader receives a computed value rather than a literal. A value carrying CR or LF ends the header section, letting the sender inject additional headers or a body that caches and clients attribute to this origin. Even without CRLF, reflecting user input into Location or Set-Cookie changes security decisions the client will make.
applicability: javascript HTTP handlers that forward identifiers, messages, or filenames into headers.
risk: HTTP response splitting and cache poisoning; MEDIUM severity.
